insight.title: Why the tallest trees never touch
insight.subtitle: A lesson in grace from the forest canopy

sections.text: Look up and see the sky through a jigsaw. In many dense forests, tree species refuse to let their branches overlap. They grow toward each other but stop just inches away. This creates winding, sunlit paths through the leaves like rivers of light. It is a quiet, leafy dance of mutual respect.

This phenomenon, called crown shyness, ensures every branch receives sunlight. By maintaining this delicate gap, trees avoid rubbing together in the wind, protecting their sensitive buds from damage. It is a calculated social distance. They share the sky without competition, allowing life to flourish in the shadows they curate.

Your day is often a series of crowded intersections. We rush and collide, forgetting the elegance of the gap. Nature reminds us that the space between things is as vital as the things themselves. Boundaries are not walls. They are the breathing room that allows everyone to find their light.

ENDING RULE:
Sometimes, the best support is to leave exactly enough room to grow.

news.title: AI model is being used to protect Artemis II from solar radiation
news.description: NASA is testing new solar radiation forecasting model on Artemis II to give astronauts earlier warnings of dangerous radiation in deep space.
news.why: This AI could help prevent outages for your GPS and internet.

news.title: Young Adults With High Blood Pressure Face Higher Risk of Heart, Kidney Disease
news.description: Recent research suggests that adults ages 30 to 40 with high blood pressure may face a higher risk of cardiovascular and kidney disease later in life. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining a healthy blood pressure at a younger age.
news.why: Monitoring your blood pressure today could prevent a future heart attack.

news.title: Time-Lapse Video Captured From Earth Shows Artemis II Spacecraft Moving Towards Moon
news.description: A striking time-lapse video shows the Artemis II Orion spacecraft, nicknamed 'Integrity', moving towards the Moon. Following its successful liftoff from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026, the spacecraft is carrying four astronauts on a historic 10-day lunar mission.
news.why: Moon mission success could lead to better satellite internet for you.

news.title: Gov't to overhaul free zones into manufacturing hubs for local production
news.description: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has announced plans to reposition Ghana’s special economic zones to support agro-processing and light manufacturing as part of a broader push to expand local industrial production.
news.why: Local manufacturing hubs may lower the price of goods you buy.

news.title: U.S. revokes legal residence status of former Iranian Guard leader Soleimani's family, takes them into ICE custody
news.description: Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter were granted U.S. asylum in 2019, but the government is now moving to strip them of their green cards.
news.why: Stricter visa enforcement could lead to more delays during your travels.
